title: Symphony No. 45 in F-sharp minor, “Farewell”
hook: A request for leave written into music, as the players stop and walk out one by one.

painting.title: The Magdalen with the Smoking Flame
painting.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
painting.pairingNote: One candle burning in a dark room, the last light left; at the end of the Farewell the players snuffed out the candles on their stands one by one, until two violins were playing by the last lights.

facts: Haydn wrote the symphony in 1772, aged forty, as music director to Prince Nikolaus Esterházy. The prince’s court spent its summers at Eszterháza, his new palace in the Hungarian countryside.

Haydn told the story himself in old age, to his biographers Griesinger and Dies. That year the stay at Eszterháza went on longer than expected, and most of the musicians had left their wives at home in Eisenstadt. Instead of asking the prince outright, Haydn put the request into the music.

In the last pages of the finale the players stop one after another, snuff out the candle on their music stand and leave, until only two muted violins are left: Haydn himself and his leader, Luigi Tomasini. The prince seems to have understood. According to the story, the court left for Eisenstadt the next day.
The key, F-sharp minor, was very unusual. This seems to be the only known symphony of the 18th century written in it, and Haydn had to order special slides so that the horns could play in it.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a fierce, driving storm (I), a slow song for muted violins (II), a quiet, hesitant minuet (III), a fast finale that breaks off and turns into the slow farewell (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro assai
movements.summary: A storm from the first bar. The violins plunge down through the notes of the minor chord while the second violins throb off the beat beneath them. There is no gentle second theme where one would expect it; instead, near the end of the middle section, the music suddenly stops for a calm new tune that is never heard again.

mainIdeas.name: The plunging theme
mainIdeas.description: the first violins race down the notes of the F-sharp minor chord, over restless, off-beat notes in the second violins and long chords in the winds.

mainIdeas.name: The new tune
mainIdeas.description: a quiet, graceful melody in the strings, in D major, almost like a minuet, which appears only once.

stops.hear: Loud and urgent: the violins plunge downwards again and again, the second violins throb beneath
stops.happening: The main theme, in the stormy style of Haydn’s [[sturm-und-drang|Sturm und Drang]] years; the throbbing is a [[syncopation|syncopation]]

stops.hear: Still restless, in another minor key: no relief yet
stops.happening: The [[exposition|exposition]] moves to C-sharp minor instead of a bright major key

stops.hear: The plunging opening again
The theme is broken up and driven through new keys
Suddenly quiet and calm: the strings play a gentle new tune in a major key
stops.happening: A new theme in D major, in the middle of the movement

stops.hear: The storm breaks again with the plunging theme

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Hard, loud chords in the minor
stops.happening: The movement closes in F-sharp minor

notice: Listen for the quiet tune at ≈ 3:00. It sounds like a moment from another piece, and Haydn never brings it back.

movements.heading: Adagio
movements.summary: A long, gentle song in A major, played by violins with mutes. Its calm keeps clouding over: the music slips into the minor and back, and slow, aching harmonies hang over from one bar to the next. Some writers hear in it the musicians’ longing for home.

mainIdeas.name: The song
mainIdeas.description: a soft, swaying melody for the [[muted|muted]] violins, with a small figure of repeated notes that sounds like a hiccup.

mainIdeas.name: The shadows
mainIdeas.description: passages that turn from major to minor and back.

mainIdeas.name: The aching chords
mainIdeas.description: notes held over into the next bar, so that the harmony clashes for a moment before it resolves.

stops.hear: Soft and veiled: the violins, muted, sing a swaying tune with little repeated notes
stops.happening: The main theme, in A major

stops.hear: The light changes: the same kind of music turns to the minor, then back
Slow, held notes that clash with the harmony underneath, then resolve
The tune wanders into darker keys
The swaying opening tune returns
The clashing, held notes again, now stretched out much longer

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The music settles quietly
stops.happening: The movement ends softly in A major

notice: Listen to the held-over notes. Each clash lasts only a moment, but when they come back near ≈ 6:20 Haydn makes them wait much longer before they resolve.

movements.heading: Menuet e Trio: Allegretto
movements.summary: A quiet, graceful [[minuet|minuet]] in F-sharp major, the bright form of the home key. It is oddly unsettled: each section stops on a weak beat, so its endings sound unfinished. The [[trio|trio]] brings the wind instruments forward.

stops.hear: A soft, courtly dance in three; the phrases end lightly, almost in mid-air
A calmer middle section; the horns and oboes come forward
The dance returns

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The last phrase stops quietly, without a firm close
stops.happening: The minuet ends on a weak beat

notice: Listen to the end of each half of the dance. The last chord falls on the third beat of the bar, the weakest, and the music seems to stop before it has finished.

movements.heading: Finale: Presto – Adagio
movements.key: F-sharp minor – A major – F-sharp major
movements.summary: The finale starts as a fast, fierce movement in F-sharp minor. When it seems about to end, it breaks off on an open chord, and a second slow movement begins in A major. One after another the players have a few last notes and leave, and the music grows thinner until two muted violins finish alone, very softly, in F-sharp major.

mainIdeas.name: The Presto
mainIdeas.description: fast, driving music in the minor, with the violins racing.

mainIdeas.name: The farewell
mainIdeas.description: a calm, gentle tune in three, in A major, played first by the whole orchestra.

mainIdeas.name: The departures
mainIdeas.description: little solos for the leaving players, in this order: first oboe and second horn, then the bassoon, second oboe and first horn, double bass, cello, the violins of the orchestra, the viola.

stops.hear: Fast and urgent: the strings drive forward in the minor
The music sounds as if it is about to end, then stops on an open, unfinished chord
Slow and calm: a gentle tune in a major key, for the whole orchestra
stops.happening: The Adagio begins, in A major

stops.hear: Short solos for the oboes and horns, then the wind instruments fall silent one by one
A short solo for the double bass, then the bass line thins
stops.happening: The double bass leaves, then the cello

stops.hear: Only violins and violas remain; the sound is light and high

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Two muted violins play alone, very softly
stops.happening: Haydn and his leader, the last two players; the symphony ends in F-sharp major

notice: On a recording you cannot see the players leave, but you can hear it. Listen for the bass disappearing and the sound growing higher and thinner.
The symphony began in a storm and ends almost in silence.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Doráti and the Philharmonia Hungarica made the first widely issued recording of all of Haydn’s symphonies for Decca, between 1969 and 1972. The orchestra had been founded in 1956 near Vienna by Hungarian musicians who had fled their country.

threads.title: Music with a message
threads.body: Haydn did not ask the prince for leave; he let the orchestra show it. The idea only works in the finale, but the whole symphony has a restless, homesick tone.

threads.title: Endings that do not end
threads.body: The minuet’s sections stop on weak beats, the Presto breaks off, and the last chord is the quietest of all.

threads.title: Storm and calm
threads.body: The fierce F-sharp minor of the first movement and the Presto frames two quiet movements, and the symphony ends in the major, very softly.
